items.text: A boat is at sea. It travels from China to San Francisco. It is going fast. It takes part in a competition . A man is on the boat. He is working. An accident happens. Wind moves the man. He falls into the water. The water is very cold. The man is not safe. His friends look for him. They must find him. They find him in one and a half hour. The man is in shock. He is very cold. Difficult words: take part (do something), competition (situation when people try to be better than others). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

An accident happened during the World Clipper Race, where competitors currently race to San Francisco from China. A competitor was changing a sail when he fell over the side of his boat. The high winds swept him away from the ship. He fell into the ice-cold water. People on the ship looked for him. It took them about one and a half hour long. The man was in shock and his body temperature was very low. Difficult words: clipper (fast ship), sail (large piece of strong cloth fixed onto a boat), sweep (move or push). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

“Mayday! Mayday! Mayday! We have a man overboard.” These chilling cries for help were called out in the early hours of Monday morning, as a British man was rescued from the Pacific Ocean, after falling overboard during the World Clipper Race. Andrew Taylor, from London, was changing a sail with a fellow crew member when he went over the side and was dunked into the ice-cold water. After being swept away from the yacht by high winds, he spent about one and a half hours in the Pacific before he was plucked from the ocean by his team-mates. Speaking back on board the boat Andrew, who is being treated for shock and hypothermia, said he feared the crew would not be able to find him. “I didn’t know if you were looking for me or not. I didn’t know if you’d see me.” “Didn’t you hear Shane shout?” “No, I heard nothing. And then I saw somebody at the mast . Initially , I thought it was a good thing because I knew you were looking for me, and then I realised that it might be a bad thing because it meant you didn’t know where I was.” The terrifying incident happened during race 10 in the 16th stage of the Round the World Race, currently racing to San Francisco from Qingdao in China. Difficult words: clipper (fast sailing ship), sail (large piece of strong cloth fixed onto a boat), dunk (fall into the water), pluck (pick up), mast (tall upright piece of wood which carries a sail), initially (in the beginning). Source: www.itn.co.uk

An earthquake hits in Chile. It happens in the north of the country. One woman says that the earthquake is strong. Everything moves. The earthquake lasts a long time, too. The earthquake makes a tsunami . People run away. They run to the mountains. Prisoners use the situation. They escape from jail. The police catch 16 of the prisoners. The police look for the rest of them. Difficult words: earthquake (when the ground moves), tsunami (very big wave), prisoner (person who is in jail). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

An earthquake struck off the coast of Chile. The quake hit near the Peruvian border. A woman said that the earthquake was strong and that everything in the old part of the city moved a lot. Another woman said that the earthquake lasted a long time. She said that all she and others could do was pray with their daughter. The earthquake triggered a tsunami. The government evacuated thousands of people from low-lying areas. Prisoners took advantage of the situation and escaped from jail. The police recaptured about 16 of the female prisoners, but security forces are still in search of the rest. Difficult words: trigger (start), take advantage (use a situation to do something you want), low-lying (place that is not high above the water), recapture (catch). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

A major earthquake has struck off the coast of Chile. The 8.2 magnitude quake hit around 100 kilometres northwest of Iquique near the Peruvian border. It triggered a tsunami with the biggest wave reported at just over two metres. At least five people have died. This woman said it was too strong and that everything in the old part of the city moved a lot. While this resident said it was very long and all they could do was pray with their daughter. There was an evacuation from the low-lying city up the mountainside and authorities said thousands of people had been on the move. The tsunami warning had been in place until early this morning. The area around Iquique has been on alert in recent weeks due to a number of tremors . It is a key copper exporting port, but firms said there had been no serious damage to the operations. Prisoners took advantage of the confusion and escaped jail. Some 16 of the women were recaptured, but security forces have been searching for the rest. Difficult words: trigger (start), tremor (small earthquake). Source: www.itn.co.uk

There is a show in a museum in New York. It is about pterosaurs. Pterosaurs live 66 million years ago. These animals can fly. However, they are not related to birds. They are related to dinosaurs. They are a unique group of animals. They are the biggest flying animals. Their wings are really big. One wing is around 5 metres long. The animals have a backbone and they can fly. This makes them really special. Difficult words: related to (like), wing (part of the body which makes the animal fly), backbone (line of bones in your back). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

There is a new exhibition at a New York museum. It is about pterosaurs. Pterosaurs were not related to bats, nor to birds. They were closely related to dinosaurs, but they were not dinosaurs. They were a unique group. These animals lived 66 million years ago. They were the first animals with backbones to evolve powered flight. They were really unique in that way. They were also the largest flying animals we know of right now. Some of the pterosaurs had wing spans up to ten meters across! Difficult words: backbone (row of bones down the centre of your back), evolve (change their bodies over time to be able to fly), wing span (size of the wings). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

The largest flying vertebrates in earth’s history are taking to the air at The American Museum of Natural History. A new exhibition at the New York museum will examine the life and history of the dinosaur era reptiles known as pterosaurs, which were the first back-boned animals to evolve powered flight. “Pterosaurs as their own unique group, they were the first animals with backbones to achieve true powered flapping flight, so that they’re really unique in that way. They also represent the largest animals we know of ever to have powered flight. Some of them have wing spans up to ten meters across, which is a huge, huge animal. But as their own group, they’re not related to birds, they’re not related to bats, they’re just a unique group of reptiles that are closely related to dinosaurs but aren’t dinosaurs. When they evolved, they were very diverse and they lived on every continent.” While the reptiles may have become extinct 66 million years ago, scientists believe that pterosaurs diversified into more than 150 species of different shapes and sizes across the planet. Difficult words: vertebrate (animal which has a backbone), reptile (cold-blooded animal), evolve (change their bodies over time to be able to fly), backbone (row of bones down the centre of your back), diverse (different), diversify (change). Source: www.itn.co.uk

Here is some news from the USA. A soldier fought in Iraq. He is not mentally OK. He is under a lot of stress . He does something bad at a military base in Texas. He drives to two buildings. He starts to shoot a gun. He kills three people. He injures sixteen people. People stop the soldier. He kills himself. This is not the first shooting at this base. There was a shooting in 2009. That shooting killed thirteen people. It injured thirty-two people. President Obama is worried about this event. Difficult words: mentally (with the mind), to be under a lot of stress (to be very unhappy), military base (place with soldiers), injure (have problems with the body). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

An American soldier drove to two buildings and opened fire at a military base in Texas. He killed three people and injured at least sixteen. Military police stopped the soldier. He then shot himself in the head. The soldier fought in Iraq and he was suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder . The military base was also the site of another shooting in 2009. In that shooting, thirteen people died and thirty-two were injured. The latest shooting is the third one at a military base in the USA in around six months. President Obama called the shooting troubling . Difficult words: open fire (begin to shoot), post-traumatic stress disorder (when a person is under a lot of stress because of something bad that happened), troubling (worrying). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

A U.S. soldier shot three people dead and injured at least 16 on Wednesday before he took his own life at the Fort Hood Army Base in Texas. The soldier, who was being treated for post-traumatic stress disorder after fighting in Iraq, drove to two buildings on the base and opened fire before he was stopped by military police. He then shot himself in the head. The incident lasted between 15 and 20 minutes. All the wounded and killed were military personnel . Fort Hood was also the site of another deadly shooting rampage in 2009 where 13 people were killed and 32 wounded. Wednesday’s shooting is the third incident at a military base in the US in around six months. President Obama has called the shooting troubling. “The folks there have sacrificed so much on behalf of our freedom. Many of the people there have been through multiple tours in Iraq and Afghanistan. They serve with valour , and they serve with distinction . When they’re at their home base, they need to feel safe.” Difficult words: wound (to injure), military personnel (people who work in military force), rampage (period of violent and uncontrollable behaviour by a person or people), folks (people), sacrifice ( to give up something to help someone), valour (great courage), distinction (excellence). Source: www.itn.co.uk

A security camera captures a crime. It happens in England. A criminal is behind a man. This man is disabled . He rides on a mobility scooter . The criminal tries to take the man’s bag. The bag gets around the man’s neck. He cannot breathe , but the criminal keeps pulling the bag. The disabled man falls on the ground. The criminal finally gets the bag. He runs away. The criminal is caught. He goes to prison. He goes to prison for 40 months. Difficult words: disabled (he cannot use a part of his body), mobility scooter (electrical moving chair for people who cannot move), breathe (get air). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

A security camera captured a shocking crime. It shows a drunk criminal who tries to steal a bag from a disabled man on a mobility scooter. It happened in England. The criminal approached to the man from behind. He tried to snatch the bag, but the bag’s cord got caught around the victim ’s neck. The victim couldn’t breathe, but the criminal did not let go of the bag. The disabled 42 year-old man fell on the ground. The 23 year-old criminal finally got the bag and ran off. The criminal was later recognised by the victim. The criminal was jailed for 40 months. Difficult words: snatch (take quickly), cord (object like a rope), victim (somebody who is attacked). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

These shocking images show the moment a drunk thug tried to steal a bag from a disabled man on a mobility scooter. CCTV footage released by police shows the moment the thug creeps up behind his victim and tries to snatch the bag from his back. The victim was hauled from his scooter and onto the ground, after the bag’s cord got stuck around his neck. Daniel Jones from Nuneaton approached the 42 year-old man when he saw him on a late night supermarket trip in Coventry. Despite the victim gasping for breath when the bag was caught around his neck, Jones refused to release his grip and dragged him off the scooter. The 23 year-old finally managed to untangle the bag’s cord and ran off. After claiming he couldn’t remember anything about the incident, he was picked out during an ID parade , and was later jailed for 40 months after admitting robbery. Difficult words: thug (criminal), creep up (to surprise somebody from behind), snatch (take quickly), haul (pull), grip (firm hold), untangle (separate something twisted), claim (say), ID parade (the victim recognised the criminal from other people). Source: www.itn.co.uk

Drug gangs in Mexico are using social media. They want to show off and fight each other. Back in 2024, a big gang breaks into two groups. Now, they are fighting for control. They use young online stars to make videos and bring in new people. But this is very dangerous. At least 19 creators die. Some creators talk about gang life only to get views. Others help hide dirty money in normal businesses. The police do not stop the killers. The danger keeps growing. Social media companies try to block bad accounts, but it is not enough to keep young people safe. Difficult words: show off (to show something proudly to make others like or support you), hide (to put something in a place where nobody can see it), danger (a situation when something bad may happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Mexico, social media is a dangerous battleground for drug cartels. Since a big cartel split into fighting groups in 2024, criminal gangs use popular influencers for propaganda , showing off power, and attracting young members. At least 19 internet stars died after being linked to criminal organizations. Some influencers make videos about drug culture for clicks, while others are investigated for helping cartels clean illegal money through private businesses and shops. Police struggle to stop the violence, and very few murders are ever solved. Social media companies try to ban bad profiles, but cartels use hidden codes to break rules. As a result, young influencers are still in danger. Difficult words: battleground (a place where a fight or war takes place), cartel (a large group of criminals), propaganda (information used to make people believe a certain idea or group). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ever since the Sinaloa Cartel split into rival groups in 2024, social media has turned into a dangerous battleground for Mexico’s drug wars. The competing factions regularly target popular content creators, and use them to show off power, post propaganda , and recruit young people. Local influencers who adopt narco culture for clicks often get caught in the middle and put themselves directly in the sights of rival gangs. On top of that, federal agents are looking into dozens of creators accused of helping cartels clean dirty money through online shops, brand deals, and live donations. This deadly connection has already cost the lives of at least 19 influencers across the country. Weak police work, a lack of real punishment, and slow moderation by tech platforms mean cartels can keep using young creators as easy tools for cash and influence online. Difficult words: faction (a small, organized group within a larger organization or political party), propaganda (information, ideas, or rumors deliberately spread to influence public opinion or promote a political cause), lack (not enough of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Canada and Europe want to work closer together. Many people in Canada prefer to buy things from Europe instead of the United States. Trade with the United States is changing. European leaders are talking about how to help each other more. They want to share energy, keep prices low, and help students study in different countries. Some big countries in Europe say that the rules are not ready for a special membership . But they still want to be strong friends. Working together helps both Canada and Europe stay safe, protect their businesses, and keep their people happy. Difficult words: share (to give a part of something to others, or to use something together), membership (when a country or person belongs to a group, club, or organization), protect (to keep someone or something safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Canada and the EU are working to build a much stronger partnership. Because of trade problems and rising costs with the United States, many Canadians prefer to buy goods from Europe and support local businesses. European leaders discussed giving Canada a special status , but some countries like Germany and France say the rules are not clear yet. Even without a formal title, Canada and the EU are already working closer together on important projects. They are sharing plans for defense , energy, clean technology, and student programs. Both sides believe that building strong relationships outside of North America will help protect their economy, keep energy supplies safe, and make their nations stronger for the future. Difficult words: status (the official position of a person, country, or organization), defense (protecting a country, building, or person against attack or harm), supply (an amount of something available to be used). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A summit in Montreal has highlighted a growing push to deepen political and economic ties between Canada and the EU. Motivated by trade disputes, geopolitical friction , and economic pressures from the United States, many Canadians are actively favoring European trade over American imports. While European Commission leadership proposed the idea of making Canada an associate member , major member states like France and Germany remain hesitant due to treaty limits and undefined legal terms. Despite these political hurdles, practical integration is already accelerating across some sectors. Canada has joined joint defense procurement programs and is exploring agreements covering energy, critical raw materials, and student exchanges. Both Canadian and European leaders view this closer partnership as essential for protecting national sovereignty, reducing dangerous dependencies on global superpowers, and securing critical supply chains in an increasingly unstable global economy. Difficult words: friction (disagreement, conflict, or tension between people or groups with different views), associate member (a member of an organization or group who has limited rights or status compared to full members), procurement (obtaining or buying goods and services, especially for a government or organization). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The EU has a new rule to save forests. The rule is starting on 30 December 2026. Companies which sell things like coffee, palm oil, and chocolate must prove that they do not cut down trees. But some big companies are still buying palm oil from places in Indonesia. People cut down forests illegally there. Some countries want Europe to stop or change the rule. These countries are, for example, the US and Indonesia. But the EU must follow the rules strictly . Indonesia is losing many trees to big fires and farming. People hope that this new rule will stop companies from harming trees and help keep the earth green and safe. Difficult words: prove (to show that something is true), illegally (against rules), strictly (exactly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The EU will start using new anti-deforestation rules on 30 December 2026. Companies which sell products like palm oil, coffee, and chocolate must prove they don’t cut down trees to make them. But environmental groups in Indonesia found that big international brands may be breaking these rules. Well-known companies like PepsiCo and Unilever recently bought palm oil from plantations linked to illegal forest clearing. Some countries, including the US and Indonesia, asked the EU to make the rules easier for businesses. But environmental activists say Europe must stay strong and enforce the law. Indonesia lost many forests to farming and fires, so strict checks are needed to protect nature and stop global forest destruction. Difficult words: anti-deforestation (about preventing or stopping the clearing of forests), brand (a product made by a company under a particular name), enforce (to make sure that a rule is followed). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The EU’s anti-deforestation law faces an enforcement test ahead of its launch on 30 December 2026. Under the new rules, companies selling goods such as palm oil, coffee, and cocoa must prove their products are not linked to land cleared after 2020. However, recent investigations by Indonesian environmental organizations reveal that major international consumer brands risk breaching these regulations. Reports show that companies like PepsiCo, Unilever, and Ferrero have bought palm oil from Indonesian plantations accused of recent illegal deforestation. Despite heavy political pressure and lobbying from major exporting nations like the United States and Indonesia to delay or soften the legislation, environmental activists insist the EU must strictly enforce the rules. Indonesia has lost vast areas of forest to illegal logging and agricultural clearing, which increased its vulnerability to severe wildfires. Experts emphasize that strict enforcement by European authorities will be essential to hold global corporations accountable and halt worldwide forest destruction. Difficult words: enforcement (compelling compliance with a law), lobby (to influence a politician or public official on an issue), vulnerability (the possibility of being attacked, damaged, or harmed). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
